articles.title: Howard Webb says accidental handball law ‘a nonsense’ and calls for reform
articles.summary: Webb wants to stop ‘ridiculous situations’ Says VAR officials in United v City had ‘tunnel vision’ Howard Webb has described the law around accidental handball as “a bit of a nonsense” and called for its reform to stop referees being drawn into “ridiculous situations”.
body: The chief refereeing officer for English football made his remarks on Tuesday, when he also fronted up over the error that allowed Manchester City to win Sunday’s Manchester derby. Webb said he was “really disappointed” with the video assistant referee call that failed to spot Enzo Fernández interfering with play from an offside position before Erling Haaland scored the only goal.

Speaking on Match Officials Mic’d Up, Webb reviewed a number of controversial incidents from the Premier League season. He said the buildup to an Ipswich own goal at Manchester United, where the ball hit Harry Maguire’s hand before he took a shot that deflected off Jacob Greaves and into the net, highlighted problems with the handball law.

“It’s a bit of a nonsense, isn’t it?” Webb said. “If [Maguire] strikes the ball beautifully into the top corner, then the goal gets disallowed. [But] he skews his shot, it becomes an own goal, and it’s awarded.”

articles.title: VAR did not even consider if Fernandez was offside - Webb
articles.summary: Referees' chief Howard Webb has admitted that the video assistant referee (VAR) did not even consider whether Enzo Fernandez was offside for Erling Haaland's controversial winner in Sunday's Manchester derby.
body: Speaking on the first edition of 'Match Officials Mic'd Up' of the season, Webb said he was "really disappointed" with the error made by the VAR Matt Donohue and his assistant Blake Antrobus.
Manchester City striker Haaland thought he had scored the only goal of the game at Old Trafford in the 60th minute, but it was disallowed on the field for offside.
A VAR review found Haaland was just onside, and the goal was awarded.

But it immediately became apparent that the video officials had made an error in failing to identify an offside offence by Fernandez, diving at the ball in a central position and interfering with opponents.

articles.title: How Kenya won its bid for 2029 World Athletics Championships
articles.summary: Kenya's athletics-loving population and improved infrastructure helped Nairobi secure the rights to host the 2029 World Championships, but challenges remain to ensure a successful event.
body: Kenya's President William Ruto says the World Athletics Championship will be "coming home", with Nairobi set to make history after being selected as the first African city to host the event in 2029.
Ruto hailed the winning bid as a "victory for generations of athletes" who have made the nation "synonymous with excellence" on the track and road.
Nairobi beat London and Rome to the hosting rights, with Munich selected to stage the 2031 edition.
After missing out on the 2025 World Championships to Tokyo, a series of factors helped Kenya see off its European rivals this time around.

articles.title: PGA Tour not planning return programme for LIV stars
articles.summary: PGA Tour chief executive Brian Rolapp says there are no plans to create an instant pathway back for LIV Golf's biggest stars after the breakaway series filed for bankruptcy protection.
body: There are no plans to create an instant pathway back to the PGA Tour for LIV Golf's biggest stars.

Major winners Jon Rahm, Bryson DeChambeau and Cameron Smith are contemplating their futures after LIV filed for bankruptcy protection last week as the breakaway league tries to create a new circuit for next year.
"There's a long legal process they have to go through before a lot of things fall into place," the Spaniard said before playing this week's BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth.
The PGA Tour is pressing ahead with its plans for a revamped set-up in 2028 but chief executive Brian Rolapp offered no guarantees that LIV's biggest names will be welcomed back.

articles.title: One of area's top quarterbacks transfers schools, will have eligibility after 30 days
articles.summary: One of the area’s top quarterbacks from last season is on the move and the landing spot is a familiar one for him. Jack Quillen, who completed 64% of his passes for 2,059 yards and 21 touchdowns as a sophomore at Warren Central, enrolled at Roncalli on Monday.
body: Under those guidelines, Quillen would be eligible for his first contest for the Week 9 regular season finale at East Central. He was previously in Roncalli’s school system through eighth grade, attending St. Jude from kindergarten through eighth grade.

“It was the right time for me to return to a faith‑based Catholic educational environment and to the community that helped shape me from kindergarten through eighth grade,” Quillen said. “I’m grateful for the experiences and relationships I built at Warren Central, and I sincerely wish my former teammates and coaches nothing but success for the remainder of their season.”

Warren Central senior Anthony Dennison, previously the backup quarterback as a junior, jumped into the starting role at the start of the year when Quillen was sidelined due to illness. Dennison is completing 59% of his passes for 867 yards and eight touchdowns (zero interceptions) for the Class 6A third-ranked Warriors, who are 4-0 going into Friday’s game vs. Ben Davis.
Quillen is a three-star prospect in the 2028 class with offers from Miami (Ohio), Toledo and UConn.

articles.title: Webb: VAR had 'tunnel vision' on Haaland which led to Enzo error
articles.summary: Pro Ref chief Howard Webb says VAR missed Enzo Fernandez being offside for Erling Haaland's winning goal in the Manchester derby due to "tunnel vision".
body: Webb says he is "really disappointed" by the decision to award the goal, which was initially ruled out on the field due to Haaland being flagged offside.
VAR then checked the incident and determined the striker was onside but failed to account for Enzo Fernandez impacting play from an offside position.

Fernandez dived for the ball before it was steered home by Haaland, and despite severely hindering Lisandro Martinez and Senne Lammens, Fernandez's offside position was overlooked once the VAR officials had confirmed he had not touched the ball - even though a player can be offside without touching the ball.
Webb told Mic'd Up: "The on-field decision was not against Fernandez; it was against Haaland. When the VAR starts their check, they see that Haaland is actually onside by three centimetres.

articles.title: Ohio State hoops legend Katie Smith to ring Victory Bell at Kent State game
articles.summary: Former Ohio State women's basketball star and current assistant coach Katie Smith will be the Victory Bell ringer before Ohio State's home football game against Kent State on Sept. 19.
body: Smith, a native of Logan, Ohio, led the Buckeyes to the NCAA Tournament championship game as a freshman in the 1992-93 season. She played in 124 games through four seasons and averaged 20.8 points, 5.7 rebounds and 3.6 assists per game on 46.9% shooting.

Along with the NCAA Tournament run, Smith was a three-time All-Big Ten guard as well as the conference's player of the year and an All-American in the 1995-96 season. The Buckeyes also made the NCAA Tournament that year, losing in the second round to No. 1 Tennessee.
After a brief stint for the Columbus Quest in the American Basketball League, Smith was drafted by the Minnesota Lynx in the 1999 WNBA player allocation draft.

Afer spending a bulk of her career with the Lynx, Smith went on to become a two-time WNBA Champion with the Detroit Shock (she was the 2008 WNBA Finals MVP) and was as a seven-time All Star in her 15-year career. Smith was inducted into the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame in 2018.

articles.title: Webb: Foden red justified but Fernandes escaped yellow for 'petulant' kick
articles.summary: Pro Ref chief Howard Webb has backed the decision to send off Phil Foden in the Manchester derby but revealed VAR could not intervene to caution Bruno Fernandes for the "petulant" kick that sparked the altercation.
body: Foden was sent off for violent conduct in Man City's 1-0 win at Old Trafford after kicking out at Fernandes after he was fouled by the Man Utd captain.
Fernandes escaped punishment after seemingly initiating the incident with a kick on Foden before the City forward reacted.
However, there appeared to be confusion during the VAR review of the incident as the officiating team checked for a possible Man Utd penalty after Enzo Fernandez's challenge on Youri Tielemans.

While referee Michael Oliver was brandishing the red card for Foden, VAR official Matt Donohue can be heard discussing the penalty while also saying: "Who has been sent off and for what?" shortly after.

articles.title: Stokes makes fifty for Durham as Surrey battle for Division One survival
articles.summary: Former England captain Ben Stokes made a half-century as Durham ended their opening day against Worcestershire 437-7 in an innings where Mayank Agarwal made a superb 177 in the County Championship.
body: Durham have already been crowned Division Two champions and secured promotion, but that did not stop them piling on the runs at The Riverside, with wicketkeeper Ollie Robinson (78 not out) also enjoying a good day with the bat.

In Division One, Surrey - battling for survival - reduced Glamorgan to 132 all out, but then mustered just 115 in reply as 20 wickets fell on the opening day at The Oval, with the visitors reaching 30 without loss in their second innings to lead by 47 runs at close of play.
At the top of the table, Ethan Bamber and Sam Hain ensured Warwickshire maintained their title challenge by ending the first day against Essex with a 17-run lead with one wicket in hand.
Seamer Bamber took six for 26 at Chelmsford to help skittle Essex for 134 and as wickets continued to tumble in Warwickshire's reply, Hain was unbeaten on 58 as the visitors closed on 151 for nine.
